subject.title: Node host: no SSH transport support + challenge auth fails behind reverse proxy

question: Should OpenClaw core own managed SSH tunnel lifecycle for `openclaw node run` and installed node services, or keep node hosts on explicit WS endpoints with external/app-managed tunnels?
rationale: The implementation is feasible with existing SSH helpers, but the decision changes remote execution security boundaries, host-key policy, credential routing, and service supervision behavior.

options.title: Design managed node SSH transport
options.body: Add a scoped node-host SSH transport that reuses the strict tunnel helper, defines host-key and cleanup behavior, and proves foreground plus installed-service upgrade paths.

options.title: Keep external tunnels only
options.body: Close or retitle the SSH part after documenting the supported manual/app-managed tunnel path and any Doctor diagnostics needed for discoverability.

options.title: Split auth follow-up
options.body: Move the direct `wss://` registration and node-approval API symptoms to the open remote-registration tracker and keep this issue focused on transport policy.

recommendation.title: Design managed node SSH transport
recommendation.body: Add a scoped node-host SSH transport that reuses the strict tunnel helper, defines host-key and cleanup behavior, and proves foreground plus installed-service upgrade paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Available local history points to steipete on the current node-host/gateway-client/SSH helper surfaces, and the decision crosses core gateway security policy.
